reviewed_items.source_claim: For an orientation-preserving pullback square f*E→E over B′→B, e(f*E)=f*e(E). For R=Z and positive rank m, reversal of orientation negates the Euler class. The ordered Whitney sum has e(E⊕F)=e(E)e(F); swapping ranks m,n changes the orientation by (−1)^(mn) and e(E)e(F)=(−1)^(mn)e(F)e(E).
reviewed_items.diagram_kind: Pullback square for an oriented bundle and Euler-class naturality
mathematical_checks: In the displayed square, the horizontal top map is the canonical pullback-bundle map f*E→E over f, both vertical maps are bundle projections, and the lower map is f:B′→B. The square commutes by the pullback construction.

The oriented pullback has Thom class pulled back from u_E; naturality of the relative-to-absolute map and the zero section gives e(f*E)=f*e(E). The displayed equality has the correct direction and domains.

For integral coefficients and m>0, reversing orientation changes the normalized Thom class by −1, hence e(E,−o)=−e(E,o). The positive-rank restriction avoids treating a rank-zero unit orientation as a second orientation.

For the ordered direct-sum orientation, the Whitney formula has no extra sign: e(E⊕F)=e(E)e(F), including the rank-zero unit. Swapping the two blocks has determinant sign (−1)^(mn); the resulting Euler-product relation agrees with graded commutativity.
